newsitem.title: USA: Tech stocks, led by Intel, push Nasdaq higher.
newsitem.headline: Tech stocks, led by Intel, push Nasdaq higher.

text.p: Technology stocks, led by heavyweight Intel Corp, powered Nasdaq shares higher.

The Nasdaq Composite Index gained 15.85 points, or 1.17 percent, to close unofficially at 1371.02. The Dow industrials rose 83.12 points, or 1.23 percent, to an unofficial close of 6823.86. The long-bond gain 14/32 to yield 6.87 percent.
"The Nasdaq opened strong, backed off a bit, but remained solid all day. The technology stocks led the day," said Brian Finnerty, senior vice president at Unterberg Harris.

Traders also said investors expressed relief at Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's briefing on the state of the U.S. economy, which suggested to many on Wall Street that interest rate policies will remain stable for the near future.

Intel's announcement it lowered first quarter prices on some microprocessor lines, while preserving prices on higher- end Pentium Pro chips lent strength throughout the semiconductor sector. Intel surged 5-3/8 to 160-1/8. Microsoft Corp gained 3-7/8 to 101-1/8, while Quantum Corp jumped 2-3/8 to 38-3/4 on better-than-expected third quarter earnings.
Jayhawk Acceptance Corp was less fortunate, dropping 4-1/2 to 3-5/8 following its quarterly results.
